dedupe_keys.name: h outbreak spatial temporal simulator of hospital infection spread and outbreaks

description: H-Outbreak is a Python simulator that generates realistic spatial and temporal data on hospitalised patients and on how a bacterial infection spreads between them. It combines an agent-based description of patients, who are admitted, move between services such as the emergency room, surgery, radiology, the intensive care unit and wards, and are discharged, with a compartmental model of infection states and with the constraints of the building: floor layout, rooms of two beds, cleaning of contaminated places and staff schedules. The provider is the author of the denissekim repository with co-authors, who describe the approach for Clostridioides difficile in Scientific Reports (2023). Coverage is a configurable hospital; the default has 212 beds. The code is on GitHub under the BSD 3-Clause licence and runs from the command line, writing patients.csv and movements.csv with the state of each patient at each step. Caveats: parameters are calibrated from the literature, not a specific hospital's data, validation in the paper is face validation and sensitivity analysis, and the repository has no tagged releases. Simulation uses: synthetic data for training outbreak detection, and testing cleaning, isolation and bed allocation policies when a hospital is under pressure. Related records: BloodPaTH (model-bloodpath) covers device-borne transmission, and Synthea (model-synthea) generates synthetic patient records.
